## Left open by the earlier read (RD-073)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L18 (Major). Problem: The lesson teaches must as a conclusion from evidence, but no worked example applies that meaning. Examples #13–#15 use requirements, advice, prohibition, and possibility only. Drawing a conclusion with must is a distinct modal-meaning case, not a change of nouns or numbers.
   > *Must* can also express a strong conclusion: "The lights are on, so someone must be home."
